Electronic programmable machine: input → storage → processing → output, under control.
Data: raw facts. Information: processed, meaningful data for decisions.
Garbage in, garbage out — output quality depends on input and program.
Babbage’s general-purpose design: store (memory) + mill (processor), punched cards.
Program and data in the same memory — von Neumann, 1945 EDVAC report.
Vacuum tubes → transistors → ICs → microprocessors → AI/parallel processing.
Working principle: analog/digital/hybrid; size: super/mainframe/mini/micro/embedded; purpose: general/special.
Control unit (decodes, directs), ALU (arithmetic and logic), registers (fast storage: PC, IR, accumulator, MAR, MDR).
Fetch → decode → execute → store, repeated billions of times a second.
Data (two-way data), address (location; 2ⁿ locations for n lines), control (read/write, clock, interrupts).
System: OS, drivers, utilities, translators, firmware. Application: general (Office, browser) and specific (CAD, GIS, CROPWAT).
Compiler: whole program before running. Interpreter: one statement at a time while running.
OCR reads printed text; OMR reads marks in boxes; MICR reads magnetic-ink characters on cheques (E-13B).
Dot-matrix (impact), inkjet, laser, thermal; plotters; 3D printers. Quality in dpi, speed in ppm.
Output that acts physically under computer control — solenoid valve, relay, motor.
